$comment: Shared CW pre-filter (noise blanker) fixture, consumed by BOTH ports: android CwPrefilterTest and ios MorseKitCheck. Data, not code - see CLAUDE.md's two-ports rule.

derivation.filter: A noise blanker on float PCM (nominal full scale +/-1), one sample in and one out, applied before the CW core. State: two second-order sections and two envelopes. All constants are in `constants`.
derivation.bandpass: RBJ constant-peak band-pass, normalised so a0 = 1: w = 2*pi*pitchHz/sampleRate, alpha = sin(w)/(2Q), b0 = alpha/(1+alpha), b2 = -b0, a1 = -2cos(w)/(1+alpha), a2 = (1-alpha)/(1+alpha), b1 = 0. y[n] = b0*x[n] + b2*x[n-2] - a1*y[n-1] - a2*y[n-2].
derivation.perSample: In this order for input x[n]: (1) detector yd = band-pass(Q = detectorQ) of x, histories shifted; (2) envelope e = max(|yd|, e*exp(-1000/(envelopeMs*sampleRate))); (3) residual r = |x - yd|, and R += (r - R) * 1000/(noiseMs*sampleRate); (4) reference = max(ratio*e, noiseRatio*R, floor) where ratio = holdRatio if a blank was already running (remaining > 0 before this sample) else triggerRatio; if r > reference then remaining = round(holdMs*sampleRate/1000); (5) blanked = remaining > 0. If blanked: remaining -= 1, the continuation resonator advances as y = g*(c*y[n-1] - y[n-2]) with c = 2cos(w), g = exp(-1000/(decayMs*sampleRate)), and its x-history takes a 0; otherwise the resonator is the band-pass (Q = resonatorQ) of x with normal history. (6) output = resonator output if blanked, else x unchanged.
derivation.retune: Changing the pitch recomputes both sections' coefficients and c; state is kept. reset() zeroes every history, both envelopes and the countdown.
derivation.vectors: signal.type tone: amplitude*sin(2*pi*pitchHz*n/sampleRate); silence: zeros; noise: uniform in [-amplitude, +amplitude) from the xorshift64* generator described in decoder.json (value = ((out >> 40) / 8388608 - 1) * amplitude). A burst adds amplitude*(1 - k/length)*(+1 for even k, -1 for odd k) at start+k, k in [0, length). Expectations: blankedAll = every sample in the inclusive range reports blanking; clearFrom = no sample at or after that index is blanked; onsetBlankBefore = every blanked sample in the vector lies before that index and there is at least one; exact = output equals input bit for bit at those indices; values = output at index n within tolerance.sample; maxAbs = |output| over [from, to) is at most max; blankedFraction = share of blanked samples over [from, to) is at most max; blankedNone = no sample blanked anywhere.
derivation.note: Values computed in double precision from these equations, not captured from either port; the ports use single precision, which the sample tolerance covers. The onset of a hard-keyed tone from silence is itself a wideband event and takes a short blank (under 2 ms); that is expected and pinned as such. Steady hiss at -20 dBFS still trips the blanker on a few percent of samples once its level is known; that is harmless (the continuation from a noise-level state decays to nothing) and pinned as a ceiling, not as zero.

vectors.name: tone passes through after its onset
crash inside a tone is blanked and the tone continues
crash inside a tone at 48 kHz
crash in silence is blanked to silence
steady hiss is left alone once its level is known
quiet room noise is never blanked
